title: Repeated-Routine vs Novelty Balance
dataSources: Photos (`photo:capture`), places visited (`location:visit`), voice memos (`voicememo:note`), logged moments (`lifelog:moment`), timeline events (`timeline:event`).
app: Life-logging and memory telemetry — photo libraries (Google Photos, Immich), location history, voice memos, and daily-moment journals — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=location:visit
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats sum(eval(if(novelty="new",1,0))) as new_places, count as total_visits by _time
| eval novelty_pct=round(100*new_places/total_visits,1)
| sort - _time
description: Shows whether your months are dominated by repeated routines or still contain a healthy amount of novelty.
value: A novelty balance metric can explain why certain months feel memorable and others blur together.
implementation: Tag location visits as new or repeat and chart monthly novelty share.
visualization: Line chart of monthly novelty percentage in visited places.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces whether life has been mostly routine lately or still includes enough new experiences to stand out.
